results.title: Power sums vanish modulo a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $e \ge 0$ be an integer such that $p - 1$ does not divide $e$ whenever $e \ge 1$. Then $p$ divides $\sum_{t=1}^{p} t^e$.

results.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and integers $a, b$, let $c_0, \dots, c_{\varphi(n)}$ be the integer coefficients of the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial, whose degree is $\varphi(n)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. The homogenized cyclotomic value is the integer

results.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value of index one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$, the homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_1(a, b)$ equals $a - b$.

results.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value of index two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$, the homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_2(a, b)$ equals $a + b$.

results.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value with second argument one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $a$, the homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_n(a, 1)$ equals $\Phi_n(a)$, the value at $a$ of the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients.

results.title: Homogenized cyclotomic value in a field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $n$ a natural number and $a, b$ integers such that the image of $b$ in $K$ is nonzero. Then the image in $K$ of the homogenized cyclotomic value $\Phi_n(a, b)$ equals $b^{\varphi(n)} \Phi_n(a/b)$, where $\Phi_n$ is the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $K$, $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, and $b$ and $a/b$ are computed in $K$.

results.title: Socialist primes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $p$ is a socialist prime if $p$ is prime, $p > 5$, and the factorials $2!, 3!, \ldots, (p-1)!$ have pairwise distinct remainders modulo $p$.

results.title: Distinct factorial residues modulo a socialist prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a socialist prime. If $a$ and $b$ are distinct natural numbers with $2 \le a \le p - 1$ and $2 \le b \le p - 1$, then $a!$ and $b!$ have different remainders modulo $p$.

results.title: Construction of measures on ℝ
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a Stieltjes function, that is, non-decreasing and right-continuous, with $f(x) \to 0$ as $x \to -\infty$ and $f(x) \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Stieltjes measure on $\mathbb{R}$. Then $\mu_f$ is a probability measure, $\mu_f((a, b]) = f(b) - f(a)$ for all real $a \le b$, and every finite measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\nu((a, b]) = f(b) - f(a)$ for all…

results.title: Construction of measures on ℝ, as unique existence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a Stieltjes function, that is, non-decreasing and right-continuous, with $f(x) \to 0$ as $x \to -\infty$ and $f(x) \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$. Then there is exactly one measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ that is a probability measure and satisfies $\mu((a, b]) = f(b) - f(a)$ for all real $a \le b$.

results.title: Satisfied clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A clause on $n$ variables is a finite set $C$ of literals $(i, b)$, where $i \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is a variable and $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. An assignment $x : \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies $C$ if $x_i = b$ for some literal $(i, b) \in C$.

results.title: $k$-SAT function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$. A Boolean function $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ is a $k$-SAT function on $n$ variables if there is a finite set $S$ of clauses on $n$ variables such that each clause in $S$ has at most $k$ literals, no two of them on the same variable, and for every assignment $x$, $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ if and only if $x$ satisfies every clause in $S$.

results.title: Positively unate variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean function and $i$ one of its $n$ variables. Then $f$ is positively unate in $i$ if for all assignments $x$ and $y$ that agree at every variable other than $i$ and have $x_i = \mathrm{false}$ and $y_i = \mathrm{true}$, $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$ implies $f(y) = \mathrm{true}$. Equivalently, switching $i$ from false to true…

results.title: Negatively unate variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ be a Boolean function and $i$ one of its $n$ variables. Then $f$ is negatively unate in $i$ if for all assignments $x$ and $y$ that agree at every variable other than $i$ and have $x_i = \mathrm{false}$ and $y_i = \mathrm{true}$, $f(y) = \mathrm{true}$ implies $f(x) = \mathrm{true}$. Equivalently, switching $i$ from false to true…

results.title: Unate Boolean function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Boolean function $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ is unate if, for every variable $i$, $f$ is positively unate in $i$ or negatively unate in $i$.

results.title: Number of $k$-SAT functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the number of Boolean functions $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that are $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables.

results.title: Number of unate $k$-SAT functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the number of Boolean functions $f : \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that are $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables and are unate.

results.title: Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture for $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the proposition that if $k \ge 2$, then the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$; that is, a $1 - o(1)$ fraction of the $k$-SAT functions on $n$ variables is unate.

results.title: Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture for all $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every natural number $k \ge 2$, the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Nearly all $k$-SAT functions are unate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the number of unate $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables divided by the number of $k$-SAT functions on $n$ Boolean variables tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$; that is, the Bollobás–Brightwell–Leader conjecture holds for every $k$.

results.title: 2-associated Stirling numbers of the second kind
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the 2-associated Stirling number of the second kind is the integer $S_2(n, k) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^j \binom{n}{j} S(n - j, k - j)$, where $S$ denotes the Stirling numbers of the second kind.

results.title: Recurrence for 2-associated Stirling numbers of the second kind
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $S_2(n, k)$ for the 2-associated Stirling number of the second kind. For natural numbers $m$ and $k$ with $1 \le k \le m$, we have $S_2(m + 2, k) = k \, S_2(m + 1, k) + (m + 1) \, S_2(m, k - 1)$.

results.title: Vanishing of 2-associated Stirling numbers of the second kind
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $n < 2k$, the 2-associated Stirling number of the second kind $S_2(n, k)$ equals $0$.

results.title: Kőnig's theorem on a finite vertex type
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a bipartite simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$. Then there are a matching $M$ in $G$ and a vertex cover $C \subseteq V$ of $G$ such that the number of edges of $M$ equals the number of vertices in $C$.

results.title: Kőnig's theorem for finite bipartite graphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every bipartite simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex type $V$ has a matching $M$ and a vertex cover $C \subseteq V$ such that the number of edges of $M$ equals the number of vertices in $C$.

results.title: Probability of a derived-allele configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Probability of the derived/ancestral configuration `x` when haplotype `i` is sampled independently and carries the derived allele with probability `q i`.

results.title: Expectation under independent haplotype sampling
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Expectation of a function `g` of the configuration under independent sampling of one haplotype per population at derived-allele frequencies `q`.

results.title: Unpolarized ABBA site-pattern indicator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Unpolarized `ABBA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `O`, `P2` with `P3`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `ABBA` and `BAAB`).

results.title: Unpolarized BABA site-pattern indicator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Unpolarized `BABA` indicator for populations `(P1, P2, P3, O)`: `P1` agrees with `P3`, `P2` with `O`, and `P1` differs from `P2` (the patterns `BABA` and `ABAB`).

results.title: Polarized ABBA site-pattern indicator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Polarized `ABBA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `O` ancestral, `P2` and `P3` derived.

results.title: Polarized BABA site-pattern indicator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Polarized `BABA` indicator (Durand et al. 2011): `P1` and `P3` derived, `P2` and `O` ancestral.

results.title: Configuration probabilities sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The configuration probabilities sum to `1`.

results.title: Sampling expectation of a product factorizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `sampleExpect` of a product of functions of single coordinates factorizes: `E[∏ i, g i (x i)] = ∏ i, (g i true * q i + g i false * (1 - q i))`.

results.title: Additivity of the sampling expectation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `sampleExpect` is additive in the function.

results.title: Sampling expectation commutes with subtraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `sampleExpect` commutes with subtraction of functions.

results.title: Sampling expectation is an expectation of independent indicators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `sampleExpect` is the expectation under independent sampling: if the derived-allele indicators `X i` are independent random variables with `P(X i = true) = q i`, then `E[g (X 0, …, X (n - 1))] = sampleExpect g q`.

results.title: ABBA–BABA site-pattern identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The site-pattern identity: `1[BABA] - 1[ABBA] = (x₁ - x₂) (x₃ - x₄)` for every configuration of derived-allele indicators.

results.title: ABBA–BABA identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: ABBA–BABA identity (Patterson et al. 2012; Durand et al. 2011): under independent sampling of one haplotype per population at derived-allele frequencies `q` (any reals; frequencies in `[0, 1]` in the biological model), `E[BABA - ABBA] = (q₁ - q₂) (q₃ - q₄)`.

results.title: Expected polarized ABBA–BABA difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Polarized form (Durand et al. 2011, with `q 3` the derived-allele frequency in the outgroup): `E[BABA_pol - ABBA_pol] = (q₁ - q₂) q₃ (1 - q₄)`. When the outgroup is fixed for the ancestral allele (`q 3 = 0`) this is `(q₁ - q₂) (q₃ - q₄)`, as in the unpolarized identity.

results.title: ABBA–BABA equals `f4`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: When the frequencies `p X ω` are themselves random (drift, and the choice of locus) and one haplotype is sampled from each population independently given the frequencies, the expected `BABA - ABBA` difference is `f4 P1 P2 P3 O`.

results.title: Linearity of the f4-statistic in its first pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Linearity of `f4` in its first pair: if `p A - p B = ∑ l, c l * (p (C l) - p (D l))` pointwise, then `f4 A B Y Z = ∑ l, c l * f4 (C l) (D l) Y Z`.

results.title: qpAdm model equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: qpAdm model equation (Haak et al. 2015, Supplementary Information): if the target `T` is an admixture of sources `S k` with weights `w k` summing to `1` (`p T = ∑ k, w k * p (S k)` pointwise; the weights may be negative, as in fitted qpAdm models), then for all `X`, `Y`, `Z`, `f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`. results.title: qpWave matrix of f4-statistics
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The qpWave matrix of left populations `L 0, …, L n` and right populations `R 0, …, R r`: entry `(i, j)` is `f4 (L (i + 1)) (L 0) (R (j + 1)) (R 0)`.

results.title: qpWave rank bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: qpWave rank bound (Reich et al. 2012, Supplementary Information; Patterson et al. 2012): if the frequency of every left population `L i` is an affine combination `∑ l, a i l * p (S l)` (`∑ l, a i l = 1`, coefficients of any sign) of the frequencies of `k + 1` source populations, then the matrix `f4 (L i) (L 0) (R j) (R 0)` (`i, j ≥ 1`) has rank at most `k`; with `k` sources, at most `k - 1`. results.title: Unbiased heterozygosity estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Unbiased estimator of `p (1 - p)` from `x` derived copies among `m` sampled copies: `x (m - x) / (m (m - 1))` (meaningful for `m ≥ 2`).

results.title: Unbiased f2 estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unbiased `f2` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix: `(â - b̂)² - â (1 - â) / (m_A - 1) - b̂ (1 - b̂) / (m_B - 1)` with `â = x_A / m_A`, written as `(x_A / m_A - x_B / m_B)² - x_A (m_A - x_A) / (m_A² (m_A - 1)) - …`.

results.title: Unbiased f3 estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unbiased `f3` estimator of Patterson et al. (2012), Appendix: `(ĉ - â) (ĉ - b̂) - ĉ (1 - ĉ) / (m_C - 1)`.

results.title: f4 estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `f4` estimator `(â - b̂) (ĉ - d̂)`; it needs no correction for four distinct populations.

results.title: Estimator of Hudson's F_ST denominator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` denominator estimator `â (1 - b̂) + b̂ (1 - â)` (Bhatia et al. 2013); the numerator estimator is `f2Hat`.

results.title: Hudson's F_ST denominator at one site
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` denominator at one site: `p_A (1 - p_B) + p_B (1 - p_A)`, the probability that two copies, one from each population, differ. The numerator is `(p_A - p_B) ^ 2`.

results.title: Hudson's F_ST (ratio of averages)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` over sites `s` in the ratio-of-averages form of Bhatia et al. (2013): `∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2 / ∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`. It is defined when the denominator is positive (it vanishes only if every site is fixed for the same allele in both populations); otherwise Lean's value `0` is a junk value.

results.title: Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At each site Hudson's numerator is at most the denominator for frequencies in `[0, 1]`: the difference is `p_A (1 - p_A) + p_B (1 - p_B) ≥ 0`.

results.title: Hudson's F_ST lies between 0 and 1
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hudson's `F_ST` lies in `[0, 1]` for frequencies in `[0, 1]`. (When the denominator vanishes the junk value `0` also lies in `[0, 1]`, so no positivity hypothesis is needed.)

results.title: Sample allele frequency is unbiased
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sample frequency is unbiased: for `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 1`, `E[X / m] = p`. (For `m = 0`, `X / 0 = 0` is a junk value, hence `m ≥ 1`.)

results.title: Unbiased heterozygosity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `X ~ Bin(m, p)` with `m ≥ 2`, `E[X (m - X) / (m (m - 1))] = p (1 - p)`.

results.title: Unbiased `f2`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Unbiased `f2` (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with independent binomial samples `X_A ~ Bin(m_A, p_A)`, `X_B ~ Bin(m_B, p_B)`, `m_A, m_B ≥ 2`, `E[f2Hat] = (p_A - p_B) ^ 2`, the population `f2` at the site.

results.title: Unbiased `f3`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Unbiased `f3` (Patterson et al. 2012, Appendix): with pairwise independent binomial samples, `m_C ≥ 2` and `m_A, m_B ≥ 1`, `E[f3Hat] = (p_C - p_A) (p_C - p_B)`.

results.title: Unbiased `f4`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For four populations sampled independently across the two pairs (`m ≥ 1` each), `E[f4Hat] = (p_A - p_B) (p_C - p_D)`; no correction is needed.

results.title: Hudson's denominator is unbiased
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hudson's denominator is unbiased (Bhatia et al. 2013): with independent binomial samples (`m ≥ 1` each), `E[hudsonDenHat] = hudsonDen p_A p_B`.

results.title: Unbiasedness of the summed f2 estimator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Summed over sites, Hudson's numerator estimator `∑ s, f2Hat` is unbiased for `∑ s, (p_A s - p_B s) ^ 2` (independence is needed only within each site).

results.title: Unbiasedness of the summed Hudson denominator estimator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Summed over sites, Hudson's denominator estimator is unbiased for `∑ s, hudsonDen (p_A s) (p_B s)`.

results.title: Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hudson's `F_ST`, ratio of averages (Bhatia et al. 2013): the ratio of the expected summed numerator and denominator estimators is the population `hudsonFst`. This is a statement about the ratio of expectations; the expectation of the ratio of the estimated sums is in general not `hudsonFst`.

results.title: The unpolarized D-statistic numerator vanishes on a tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the drift model, if no edge lies on both the `P1–P2` and the `P3–O` path (as on the tree `((P1, P2), P3), O`), then the expected unpolarized `ABBA` and `BABA` counts are equal. Thus `BABA - ABBA` and its sign reversal have expectation `0`. The integrability hypotheses make both expectations meaningful.

results.title: qpAdm model equation in the drift model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the lineage weights of `T` are an affine combination `∑ k, w k • weight (S k)` of those of the sources (`∑ k, w k = 1`, weights of any sign), then `f4 T X Y Z = ∑ k, w k * f4 (S k) X Y Z`.
